records.title: Attack 1 · Target was 5,000 ton freighter, similar to BOSTO

fields.description: Target was 5,000 ton freighter, similar to BOSTON MARU, ONI 208-J P.211 (5450 tons). It had been seen at bauxite loading pier and was proceeding from pier to MALAKAL HARBOR, PALAU via AIWOKAKO pass and TOAGEL MLUNGUI pass. It was hugging reef closely and was escorted by one patrol boat. Due to squally weather, target was not seen to leave loading pier until it had almost reached AIWOKAKO pass.
fields.damage determined by: Of the four torpedoes fired, three were heard to de- finitely explode on the reef. The fourth torpedo was either a dud or low order explosion, being heard by only the sound operator.

fields.narrative:
Fired four torpedoes. Range 3300 yds, 125 stbd. track, gyro angle zero, 1 divergent spread. ATTACK 1.
1432-18 Fired 1 tube.
1432-27       2 tube.
1432-35       4 tube.
1432-44       ⟦3⟧ tube.
1436-43 Heard faint explosion on sound.
1437-37 heard loud torpedo explosion.
1437-53   "    "      "         "
1438-17   "    "      "         "
After firing, went deep, as at least one torpedo was seen smoking badly and patrol boat was seen to turn toward us. Did not see ex- plosions. It is believed all torpedoes hit the reef, probably about 2. mile north of TOAGEL MLUNGUI.

fields.narrative:
ATTACK 2.
0157-40 Fired 7 tube.
0157-52 Fired 8 tube.
These two torpedoes were fired with a snap set up at a tanker as we were clearing convoy at full speed, estimated range 600 yds, 90 stbd. track. While firing second torpedo, noted target changing course so checked fire. A torpedo hit was heard 2 min 20 sec after firing 7, which indicates a hit on a ship in the port or far column. At time of firing, PPI indicated several ships in line of fire. Rain at the time reduced visibility below 3000 yds. This hit also confused the escorts, as they apparently all headed to the vicinity of the ship that had been hit and depth charged the vicinity for several hours. It is be- lieved that excessive speed, coupled with short range, resulted in torpedoes under running intended target.

fields.narrative:
ATTACK 8.
0502-08 Fired 1 tube, 145° stbd. track, range 2050 yds.
0504-08 Hit square amidships that broke its back. Target was a passenger freighter.
0512 Saw target sink. Radar pip disappeared. Radar screen was now clear, indicating that there were probably no ships within ten miles. Dawn was rapidly approaching. Secured from battle stations. SILVERSIDES has had herself a busy night of it, firing 19 torpedoes in about three hours. If time had not been pressing, attacks could have been made more deliberately and more hits obtained. Would have "enjoyed" this convoy more if had been able to spread the attack over two nights. The Commanding Officer desires to commend -- the officers and crew all did their job well. The control party functioned smoothly. Lt-Comdr. BASLEY, assistant in command and the ass't TDC operator. Lt Worthington quickly analyzed the set-ups on the TDC and set them up accurately. Lt. Kane watched the PPI and supplied accurate ranges and bearings to control party and bridge. Lt. Nichols manned the TBT continuously despite difficult conditions. Lt(jg) Parker plotted continuously from the time contact was first establish- ed. Lt. Cielesz and Lt(jg) Reidel kept things organized below, continuously compensating so that we could dive at any minute and had perfect trim when did make a dive later. Ensign Smiley was busy going from one torpedo room to the other supervising the firing and the reloads which were made in record time. The Commanding Officer, who at the time was too busily engaged watching a nearby escort, did not intentionally allow the ship to get in the dangerous position in the middle of the convoy. Luck and Mr. Fairbanks Morse got us out of that spot.

fields.event: O.O.D. Lt. Malone, sighted impulse bubble and torpedo wake bearing 160 T, range of bubble about 1200 yds. Torpedo coming in on abot a 120 stbd. track OOD swung left with full rudder and went ahead emergency. Torpedo passed about 50 yds down stbd. beam. Another torpedo was seen to the right of this one, passing about 150 yds. down stbd. beam. Last torpedo fired came down port side, distance about 75 yards. Lt. Malone deserves much credit for his prompt and correct action. After firing, could see periscope astern. The Jap deserves credit for his periscope handling. Sea was calm, with some ripples and no whitecaps. SILVERSIDES had been zigzagging, keeping an all-around lookout with both periscopes plus 4 lookouts and 2 officers on the bridge. A possible sound approach is indicated. SHIP CONTACT # 16.

Torpedoes were fired with a 65 stbd. track, range 1840 yds, gyro 184-187. Target was large tanker and he filled the field of 7 x 50 binoculars.

0300-08 " " "

Explosions do not check with torpedo run. Sound heard an explosion which checked about right but time was not recorded. Lt. Nichols on TBT, saw one big splash near bow of target. Commanding Officer was looking for escort. Radar later reported size of target pip decreasing but this could be due to target changing course. About time explosions were heard, target zigged away. Escort again chose wrong side and dashed over to port side of convoy, dropping charges. Weather was probably too rough to shoot and some of the fish ran erratic. It is probable that target was damaged, although evidence is inconclusive.

Sent SEADRAGON convoy's position, course and speed via radio Guadalcanal and NPM. Message transmitted on Fox schedules about two hours later.

Radar again in operation. Convoy bears 232 T, distance 12,800 yds. During the night, from 2107 to 0037 heard occasional depth charges at various intervals, indicating SEADRAGON was in contact with something, or that convoy was celebrating its closeness to TRUK by splurging and dropping embarrasing depth charges.
